own_solution.law: T = 2 pi sqrt(d0/g), d0 = rho_b h/rho_l = 0.195 m

defect_reasons.invalid_parameter_domain: Every listed radius (2.5, 4.5, 7 cm) is far below the r > 20 cm needed (r^2 > 2 d0 (h - d0) = 0.041 m^2) for a 30 cm cylinder of relative density 0.65 to float upright stably, so the C sentences contradict the authors' own assumption that the cylinder floats upright and moves only vertically.
defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The cylinder is never called wooden, so 'the same wood' in T315E/T4379 may refer to the raft's wood of unstated density; the R answers silently assume density 650 kg/m^3.

counterexamples: r = 7 cm (largest listed): GM = d0/2 + r^2/(4 d0) - h/2 = 0.0975 + 0.0063 - 0.15 = -0.046 m < 0; the upright cylinder tips over, so no vertical bobbing occurs.
notes: Numerical claims verified: base 2 pi sqrt(0.195/9.8) = 0.8863 s; R at 3.5, 9.5, 14 cm gives 0.9366, 1.0170, 1.0734 s; K regime min(19.5, 10.5) cm > 1.1, 3.2, 3.8 cm holds. D sentences (raft, earlier run) and minimal pairs (TF10E/T4379, TFE49/T315E, numeral-free twins) are as intended. The cancellation of the radius is algebraically right, but the radius values put the stated configuration outside the domain where an upright float exists; agreement with pass 1.
